newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen unmoved by Kolodko exit.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen unmoved by Kolodko exit.

text.p: Polish shares inched up, apparently little moved by Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko's resignation on Tuesday, and analysts said the bourse was likely to keep moving independently from the news, probably downward.
The main market's WIG index rose 0.1 percent, to 16,525.2, and turnover rose 27.5 percent to 182.5 million zlotys ($60.8 million) on both markets as 38 issues rose, 29 fell and 20 were flat.

"I think the market will move fairly independently from the announcement of Kolodko's resignation," said Stephen Pettyfer, an analyst at Merrill Lynch, but added the market would carefully watch the policy of Kolodko's successor, Marek Belka.
Analysts said the bourse would likely fall in the next few sessions, but that the falls would be due to profit-taking after recent rises rather than Kolodko's resignation.
The bourse surged 27 percent from mid-December to late January and after a four-session correction it jumped 2.5 percent on Monday.
Some analysts said last week's correction bottom of 16,105.5 points of the WIG index should provide strong support, but others saw the index falling to 15,000.
Some said the market looked overheated, with some stocks, mainly in the computer and food sectors, trading at high P/Es.
Bank Ochrony Srodowiska fell 4.2 percent in profit-taking after it debuted on Monday 65.5 percent higher than its issue price, traders said.
Cable maker Kable jumped 6.4 percent, extending Monday's gain on news that Denmark's NKT Cables plans to increase its stake in the firm to over 50 percent.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 1.7 percent in 21.7-million-zloty ($7.2 million) trade in the regular session and fell one percent in 10-million-zloty ($3.3 million) continuous trade.
